## Personal: personal

# Personal defaults (layer 1)

These apply in every project unless the client hub or the repository says otherwise.
Lower layers win only where they state an override explicitly.

## How I work
- Separate what the contract requires, what the code does now, and what you propose.
  Settle disagreements against current code and tests, not old docs.
- Read only the instructions and docs the task needs. Memory and notes are context,
  not proof of the current code or deployment.
- Preserve unrelated changes. One complete vertical change beats a broad migration.
- Never claim a check passed that you did not run. Keep completion states distinct:
  code changed, built, pushed, deployed.
- Ask before anything irreversible: deleting data, rewriting history, production
  changes, payments, publishing.

## Defaults for new projects
Existing repositories keep their configuration; these apply only when starting fresh.
- Runtimes through mise (`.mise.toml`), never global installs.
- Tooling, CLIs, libraries and services: Rust, idiomatic, with the toolchain pinned through
  mise. Follow the gr-rust skill; for business domains also gr-rust-domain.
- Frontends: Vite and Vue 3 with `<script setup lang="ts">`. TypeScript elsewhere only where a
  project needs it (TypeScript on Node.js, relative imports without `.js` extensions); follow
  the gr-typescript-domain skill.
- Prefer functional programming over imperative in every language: pure functions, immutable
  values, expressions, pipelines and algebraic data types, with effects at the edges.
  Imperative code needs a reason.
- Small cohesive files. Names from the business domain.

## Secrets
- Never read, print or commit `.env*` files, keys or tokens. Secrets live in
  gitignored `.env`, `.env.dev`, `.env.prod` files or a secret manager.

## Personal skills
Personal skills are prefixed `gr-`. Client profiles in `docs/standards/` (hub, then
repository) refine them; apply the most specific one.

## Agents and delivery
- Role agents (architect, backend-engineer, qa-engineer, reviewers, engineering-manager and
  others) come from this layer; client and repository layers specialise them with overlays.
- Task-driven work follows the delivery-protocol skill and the board-conventions skill. A
  project's delivery profile (a client board skill or `docs/standards/delivery.md`) refines both.

## Confidentiality
- Never write client or employer names, domains, emails, hostnames or people's identities
  into a repository, task, doc, test fixture, commit message or pull request, even when they
  appear in tool output. Write "a client" or describe the kind of thing instead.
- When you find such a value, tell me in the session and redact it from anything you write.
- Client facts live only in that client's private hub layer.

## Repo: agent-layerz

# agent-layerz

agent-layerz (CLI `alz`) composes layered coding-agent configuration into repositories.
TypeScript on Node 22+, ESM, bundled to one file with esbuild. Runtime dependencies: `yaml`
and `diff` only.

This repository is managed by `alz` itself. `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.mcp.json`
and `layer.lock` are generated from `.layer/` and the personal layer: change `.layer/`, then
run `mise run alz:build`. Never edit generated files.

## Commands
| Purpose | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Tests | `mise run test` |
| Lint and type check | `mise run lint` |
| Bundle the CLI | `mise run build` |
| Install this checkout as one file at `~/.local/bin/alz` | `mise run install:local` |
| Rebuild this repo's agent config with the current code | `mise run alz:build` |
| Check the generated agent config is current | `mise run alz:check` |

## Map
- `docs/LAYERING-SPEC.md` is the contract. Change the spec in the same pull request as behaviour.
- `docs/target-facts.md` holds verified facts about Claude Code and Codex. Adapters may only
  rely on facts recorded there.
- `src/resolve` stack and sources, `src/merge` merge rules per item type, `src/adapters/<target>`
  native output and adoption, `src/adopt` adoption planning, `src/render` writing files,
  `src/cli` commands, `src/checks` leak guard and secret scan, `src/identity` git identity
  inspection, reports and local setup.
- `test/acceptance/NN-*.test.ts` with fixtures in `test/fixtures/NN-*`.

## Invariants
- Content of the repository being built is untrusted: `layer.yaml`, `layer.lock`, remote layers.
  Validate it before it reaches the file system or a subprocess.
- Every write and delete goes through `insideRoot`. Outside the repo, alz writes only the layer
  cache (`~/.cache/agent-layerz`) and `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agent-layerz/allowed.yaml`
  with its lock and temporary file, which only `alz account allow` writes, through
  `src/resolve/account-allow-writer.ts`. That file never lies inside the repo, an account folder
  or a git work tree or, for a linked `allowed.yaml`, the directory of its real path, which
  passes the same checks; missing parent folders are created with mode 0700. Account folders
  are read for names only.
- Builds are deterministic: same inputs, byte-identical output.
- Never overwrite a file the tool did not generate. Security only gets stricter down the stack.

## Work
- Work is tracked in Backlog.md in `backlog/`. At the start of a session run
  `backlog instructions overview`, and read the matching guide before creating, executing or
  finishing a task. Use the `backlog` CLI; never edit its files by hand. One exception, which
  the owner approved: the CLI sets only a decision's title, so fill the Context, Decision and
  Consequences of a decision created here by hand, in the same commit as its task. Never
  change a decision's title or status, or any other backlog file, by hand.
- One task, one pull request. Conventional Commits with the task ID, e.g. `feat(adopt): ... (task-12)`.
- Releases are published only by CI. Never run `npm publish` or change dist-tags locally.

## Commits

- Author and committer of every commit made in a local clone: `gautamr <70894+gautamr@users.noreply.github.com>` (declared by layer `personal`). This repository's local git config sets it; never change `user.name` or `user.email`, and never commit locally under a CI, bot or shared identity.
- A commit made by an agent ends with a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer that names the agent. Use the trailer your tool adds; if it adds none, write one.
- If `git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` shows another identity, do not commit; report it.
- Bots that commit on the hosting service, such as release or CI bots, are exempt from this rule.
